publicReleaseNotes: Penny 0.2.2 keeps the operator Feedback page readable during a workspace export: on RER Managed, GET /app/feedback no longer fails while Export workspace or Download backup holds the data lock, and the pause notice is scoped to Feedback and clears when the export is finished or aborted. It also adds email capture to a dedicated address (CAP-009), requester Google and GitHub sign-in (REQ-039), rule-based redaction of sensitive evidence before storage (AI-008, partial) and cited evidence summaries and reply drafts (AI-006), with operator form, navigation and upload-limit fixes. Migrations 0088 to 0091 are additive and the new features stay off until the owner configures them. It runs on rer 0.2.77. Local setup and dev on a Platform-migrated database, SendGrid duplicate suppression, hosted Email Routing, real Google and GitHub consent, live external feedback providers and whole-product acceptance beyond the proved core loop remain known limits. Product screenshot: public/brand/releases/penny-0.2.2-1440.png

CAP-009.summary: Dedicated email capture ships against provider-edge fixtures: one inbox item per Message-ID from operators or allowlisted DMARC-aligned senders, forwarders kept as admitted-sender provenance, direct or BCC copies marked not forwarded, replay digests kept after erasure, refusals kept as counts, HTML-only mail refused; hosted Email Routing and live mail are not run.
CAP-009.was: Each installation has a dedicated capture address on the owner's domain (Cloudflare Email Routing or the configured mail provider's inbound parse). Operators forward or BCC customer emails to it. Penny accepts only mail from operator addresses or allowlisted domains with DMARC alignment, recovers the original sender from the forwarded message, keeps attachments within `seed.json` limits and creates one inbox item per message ID. Notification reply addresses never reach this route, and it refuses mail from Penny's own sender addresses (`MAIL_FROM` and any NOTIFY-013 sender), as NOTIFY-004 requires. *Acceptance:* Inbound-mail fixtures: forwarded Gmail and Outlook messages each create one item attributed to the original sender; a replayed message ID, an unaligned sender, mail from Penny's own sender address and a reply to a Penny notification create nothing.
CAP-009.now: Each installation has a dedicated capture address on the owner's domain (Cloudflare Email Routing or the configured mail provider's inbound parse). Direct or BCC copies without recoverable forwarded headers are attributed to the admitted sender and marked not forwarded. Message-ID digests stay after erasure so a replay cannot recreate an item. Refusals keep only non-personal reason counts. Hosted Email Routing, a real domain and live mail acceptance: NOT RUN. Admission depends on the `Authentication-Results: mx.cloudflare.net;` header, which only a hosted receipt can confirm. HTML-only mail is refused (`excerpt_size_or_plain_text_required`). Captured source provenance records "Forwarded by <admitted sender>"; a recovered body address is labeled "Sender stated in forward".

AI-006.summary: Cited summaries and reply drafts read only records the current operator can see under AI-010's data-processing setting, drop unresolvable citations with a notice, post replies only as operator-edited public comments after a fresh private-value check, and refuse a draft completed after its session was revoked.
AI-006.was: For a request, decision or account, Penny drafts a cited summary of its evidence and discussion; for comments and inbox items it drafts a reply or status-update wording that an operator edits and sends. Drafts never send themselves, and a draft carrying a private value (an account name, revenue, an internal note) is flagged before publication (EVID-006). *Acceptance:* Every citation in a fixture summary resolves to a stored record; a draft containing a private account name is flagged; nothing is sent without the operator's action.
AI-006.now: For a request, decision or account, Penny drafts a cited summary of its evidence and discussion; for comments and inbox items it drafts a reply or status-update wording that an operator edits and sends. Drafts never send themselves, and a draft carrying a private value (an account name, revenue, an internal note) is flagged before publication (EVID-006). Drafting reads only records available to the current operator; the prompt obeys AI-010’s data-processing setting. Unresolvable citations are dropped with a visible notice and never displayed as cited. Replies today are public request comments, posted only after the operator edits and posts; this draft feature sends no email or connector reply. Unlinked inbox drafts remain editable until linked to a published request. Future connector and mail replies under NOTIFY-007, CAP-003, CAP-004, CAP-005, CAP-006, CAP-019 and CAP-009 inherit the operator edits and sends, never auto-send, and a fresh private-value check before publication. AI-011 carries measured quality (none of its evaluation bars apply to this clause); ROLE-001 carries the missing restricted-commercial-field roles, including draft context and publication checks. These inherited obligations do not narrow the shipped drafting flow. *Acceptance:* Every citation in a fixture summary resolves to a stored record; unknown citations are dropped and disclosed; a draft containing a private account name is flagged and its publication refused until edited; nothing is sent without the operator's action. A revoked session refuses a draft completed in flight.

AI-008.summary: Deterministic rule-based redaction before storage ships for operator evidence, CAP-009 email capture and portal submissions, with owner-confirmed reapplication over at most 200 evidence wording versions; model detection, saved-import originals, learning source envelopes and binary attachments remain open.
AI-008.was: Owner-configured rules (US Social Security numbers, payment card numbers, phone numbers, email addresses, credential shapes and custom patterns), with optional model detection, redact captured excerpts and transcripts before storage; redactions are marked, and the unredacted original stays only in the source system. *Acceptance:* `pnpm run eval:ai -- --set redaction-v1` (AI-011) reports recall of at least 0.99 for Social Security and payment card numbers and at least 0.95 for the other default kinds, with precision of at least 0.90; a fixture ticket containing an SSN and a card number is stored redacted in D1, search and the archive; a new rule applies to new captures and, on request, re-applies to stored ones.
AI-008.now: Owner-configured rules (US Social Security numbers, payment card numbers, phone numbers, email addresses, credential shapes and custom patterns), with optional model detection, redact captured excerpts and transcripts before storage; redactions are marked, and the unredacted original stays only in the source system. *Acceptance:* `pnpm run eval:ai -- --set redaction-v1` (AI-011) reports recall of at least 0.99 for Social Security and payment card numbers and at least 0.95 for the other default kinds, with precision of at least 0.90; a fixture ticket containing an SSN and a card number is stored redacted in D1, search and the archive; a new rule applies to new captures and, on request, re-applies to stored ones. *Status:* This is a deterministic rule-only implementation; optional model detection is not built and AI-010 is unchanged. Binary attachments are not rewritten. Operator evidence, CAP-009 email capture and native portal submission use guarded before-storage rules. AI-011 remains missing and inherits extending the minimal redaction-v1 runner. Gap: saved-import originals and learning source envelopes are not redacted before storage. Explicit reapplication currently covers at most 200 evidence wording versions, not every stored transcript or copied request field; larger stores need paged reapplication. The full before-storage and reapplication promises remain open.

NOTIFY-004.summary: The Worker accepts inbound mail only through CAP-009's platform-invoked email handler, which refuses Penny's own senders, a configured reply-to and notification replies; no HTTP route accepts a posted mail message.

NOTIFY-013.was: Owners and Admins set, in settings, how requester and release email presents the business, as Canny's email whitelabeling does: the sender name (default: the INT-007 company name), the from address on a domain verified with the owner's mail provider (Penny sends a test message to the operator and shows the provider's result before saving, and refuses an address the provider rejects), an optional monitored reply-to address that is never the CAP-009 capture address (without one, replies go to the no-reply address under NOTIFY-004), and the business postal address. Every requester and release email (NOTIFY-001, NOTIFY-008–NOTIFY-012, REL-005, REQ-030's rejection notice) uses the sender name and from address and carries the postal address in its footer with the one-click unsubscribe, as CAN-SPAM requires. First-run setup (OPS-005) asks for the postal address with the company name and cannot finish without both; an installation set up earlier shows its owner a one-time prompt alongside OPS-008's. Until a postal address is recorded, the paths that email people who did not ask in that moment cannot be turned on or chosen, each refused with the reason: vote subscriptions (NOTIFY-008), author subscriptions (NOTIFY-011), the captured-contact send (NOTIFY-009), the weekly digest (NOTIFY-010) and MIG-007 carry-over; boards created meanwhile start with vote subscriptions off; mail a requester explicitly asked for (a follow, an Email me updates tick, an updates subscription) still sends; and the overview shows the missing address until it is set. Operator email (NOTIFY-003, NOTIFY-006) uses the same from address and needs no postal address. Company and postal setup, the legacy confirmation prompt, provider-tested sender acceptance and refusal, configured sender and reply-to headers, the postal footer and automatic-subscription admission ship, with route, HTTP-edge provider fixtures and 1440/390 browser proof.
